papers.title: LinearCapR: Linear-time computation of per-nucleotide structural-context probabilities of RNA without base-pair span limits
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation RNA molecules adopt dynamic ensembles of secondary structures, where the local structural context of each nucleotide–such as whether it resides in a stem or a specific type of loop–strongly shapes molecular interactions and regulatory function. Structural-context probabilities therefore provide a more functionally informative view of RNA folding than the minimum free energy structures or base-pairing probabilities. However, existing tools either require O ( N 3 ) time or employ span-restricted approximations that omit long-range base-pairs, limiting their applicability to large and biologically important RNAs. Results We introduce LinearCapR, enabling linear-time, span-unrestricted computation of structural-context marginalized probabilities, using beam-pruned Stochastic Context Free Grammar-based computation. LinearCapR retains global ensemble features lost by span-limited methods and yields superior predictive power on bpRNA-1m(90) dataset, especially for multiloops and exterior regions, as well as long-distance stems. LinearCapR supports analysis of long RNAs, demonstrated on the full genome of SARS-CoV-2. LinearCapR provides the first base-pair-span-unrestricted, linear-time framework for RNA structural-context analysis, retaining key thermodynamic ensemble features essential for functional interpretation. It enables large-scale studies of viral genomes, long non-coding RNAs, and downstream analyses such as RNA-binding protein site prediction. Availability and Implementation The source code of LinearCapR is available at https://github.com/hoget157/LinearCapR . The archived software release used in this work is available at Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19450645

papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要与动机**  
RNA分子会呈现出多种动态的二级结构组合，其中每个核苷酸所处的局部结构环境——例如它是否位于茎部或某种特定类型的环结构中——会显著影响其分子间的相互作用及其功能。因此，基于结构环境的概率分析能够比仅依赖最小自由能结构或碱基配对概率的方法，提供更多关于RNA折叠功能的信息。然而，现有的工具要么需要O(N³)级别的计算时间，要么采用范围受限的近似方法来忽略长距离的碱基配对，这使得它们难以应用于大型且具有生物学意义的RNA分子。  

**研究结果**  
我们提出了LinearCapR这一工具，它利用基于束剪随机上下文无关文法的计算方法，实现了线性时间内、无范围限制的结构环境概率分析。与那些采用范围受限方法的工具相比，LinearCapR能够保留所有全局结构特征，在bpRNA-1m(90)数据集上表现出更强的预测能力——尤其是在处理多环结构、外部区域以及长距离茎部结构时。该工具已成功应用于SARS-CoV-2的全基因组分析，证明了其适用于长链RNA的研究。LinearCapR为RNA的结构环境分析提供了首个无范围限制、线性时间的计算框架，同时保留了那些对功能解析至关重要的热力学特性。这一工具为大规模研究病毒基因组、长非编码RNA以及进行RNA结合蛋白位点预测等下游分析奠定了基础。  

**开源与实现方式**  
LinearCapR的源代码可访问https://github.com/hoget157/LinearCapR获取。本研究所使用的软件版本已存档于Zenodo平台，链接为：https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19450645。

all_papers.title: LinearCapR: Linear-time computation of per-nucleotide structural-context probabilities of RNA without base-pair span limits
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation RNA molecules adopt dynamic ensembles of secondary structures, where the local structural context of each nucleotide–such as whether it resides in a stem or a specific type of loop–strongly shapes molecular interactions and regulatory function. Structural-context probabilities therefore provide a more functionally informative view of RNA folding than the minimum free energy structures or base-pairing probabilities. However, existing tools either require O ( N 3 ) time or employ span-restricted approximations that omit long-range base-pairs, limiting their applicability to large and biologically important RNAs. Results We introduce LinearCapR, enabling linear-time, span-unrestricted computation of structural-context marginalized probabilities, using beam-pruned Stochastic Context Free Grammar-based computation. LinearCapR retains global ensemble features lost by span-limited methods and yields superior predictive power on bpRNA-1m(90) dataset, especially for multiloops and exterior regions, as well as long-distance stems. LinearCapR supports analysis of long RNAs, demonstrated on the full genome of SARS-CoV-2. LinearCapR provides the first base-pair-span-unrestricted, linear-time framework for RNA structural-context analysis, retaining key thermodynamic ensemble features essential for functional interpretation. It enables large-scale studies of viral genomes, long non-coding RNAs, and downstream analyses such as RNA-binding protein site prediction. Availability and Implementation The source code of LinearCapR is available at https://github.com/hoget157/LinearCapR . The archived software release used in this work is available at Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19450645

all_papers.primary_summary_raw:
MOTIVATION: RNA molecules adopt dynamic ensembles of secondary structures, where the local structural context of each nucleotide-such as whether it resides in a stem or a specific type of loop-strongly shapes molecular interactions and regulatory function. Structural-context probabilities therefore provide a more functionally informative view of RNA folding than the minimum free energy structures or base-pairing probabilities. However, existing tools either require O(N3) time or employ span-restricted approximations that omit long-range base-pairs, limiting their applicability to large and biologically important RNAs.

RESULTS: We introduce LinearCapR, enabling linear-time, span-unrestricted computation of structural-context marginalized probabilities, using beam-pruned Stochastic Context Free Grammar-based computation. LinearCapR retains global ensemble features lost by span-limited methods and yields superior predictive power on bpRNA-1m(90) dataset, especially for multiloops and exterior regions, as well as long-distance stems. LinearCapR supports analysis of long RNAs, demonstrated on the full genome of SARS-CoV-2. LinearCapR provides the first base-pair-span-unrestricted, linear-time framework for RNA structural-context analysis, retaining key thermodynamic ensemble features essential for functional interpretation. It enables large-scale studies of viral genomes, long non-coding RNAs, and downstream analyses such as RNA-binding protein site prediction.

AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: The source code of LinearCapR is available at https://github.com/hoget157/LinearCapR. The archived software release used in this work is available at Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19450645.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

all_papers.summary: We developed a foundation model for 3D genome organization from Hi-C-derived chromatin structure. HiCFoundation supports integrative analysis linking genome architecture to downstream regulatory function. Through large-scale self-supervised pretraining on Hi-C data, followed by fine-tuning on downstream tasks, it provides a unified, efficient, generalizable and interpretable paradigm for 3D genome, single-cell and multiomics analysis across species

llm_highlights_zh: HiCFoundation支持将基因组结构与下游调控功能进行整合分析。
通过在Hi-C数据上进行的大规模自我监督预训练，随后在下游任务中进行微调，该方法为跨物种的3D基因组分析、单细胞研究以及多组学分析提供了一种统一、高效、具有泛化能力且易于解释的分析框架。

all_papers.llm_rss_summary_zh: 我们基于Hi-C技术获得的染色质结构数据，开发了一个用于分析三维基因组组织的基础模型。该模型能够将基因组的空间结构与下游的调控功能联系起来，进行综合分析。通过在大量Hi-C数据上进行自监督预训练，随后针对具体应用任务进行微调，该模型为跨物种的三维基因组分析、单细胞研究以及多组学数据分析提供了一种统一、高效、具有普遍适用性且易于解释的分析框架。
